answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the opal hash is checked against the gale checkpoint at intake, the horizon audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 262 aliases cost 262 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
